The job leaks `inventory-sync` whenever the supplier request or later database work throws. `$lock->release()` is only reached after successful completion, so an outage leaves the Redis lock held until its 300-second TTL. Retries then see the lock and return as “skipped,” masking the original failure. The existing tests cover success and contention, but not exception cleanup.
Wrap all post-acquisition work in `try/finally`, releasing the lock in `finally`; alternatively use Laravel’s lock callback API, which releases automatically. This also protects against database/update exceptions, not just supplier failures. The 300-second TTL means the current defect is technically temporary per lock, but repeated failed attempts can continually renew the blockage and make recovery appear permanent.
<diagnosis>
Root cause: `SyncSupplierInventory::handle()` acquires the cache lock but releases it only on the success path. Mechanism: `Http::get()->throw()` propagates the supplier outage exception before `release()`, leaving the Redis lock owned until its 300-second expiry; queued retries encounter that lock and return as skipped, while later failed acquisitions can repeat the cycle. Fix: put the complete sync operation inside a `try/finally` after successful acquisition, releasing the lock in `finally` (or use Laravel’s lock callback helper), and add an exception-path test asserting that a failed sync does not prevent the next sync.
</diagnosis>
